pr_title: backupccl: restore database into a new named database
pr_body:
Previously, if a user had a problematic database in their cluster that they
wanted to restore from backups, but also wanted to maintain traffic to the db
during the restore, the user had to rename the active database and point the
application to the renamed db, which can be cumbersome.

This change adds a restore option, 'new_db_name', allowing the user to apply a
new name to the restoring database, during single database restores.

Fixes: #67927

Release Note (sql change): Added the optional new_db_name clause to RESTORE
DATABASE statement, allowing the user to rename the database they intend to
restore.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/70222)

issue_context.title: bulk: restore database into a new named database
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If I have an issue with a database, but want to keep it around as I'm restoring / keep application traffic going, I don't have a great way to do it today. I have to rename that database and point my application to a newly named database so that I can restore that old database, then change application back.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
`RESTORE DATABASE d1 FROM 'file' WITH new_db_name=d1_new`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
`RESTORE DATABASE d1(into=d1_new), d2(into=d2_new) FROM 'file'`

We need to lock in syntax (cc @livlobo )

Epic: CRDB-6767
comments:
@livlobo @mwang1026 I want to kickstart a bikeshed of the syntax. @msbutler I think this would be an interesting introduction to restore, now that you have dabbled in backup!

How does `rename_db` sound as the option name?

review_comments: I know we discussed this offline but I see no reason not to validate some of these options that can only be used with certain flavours of restore much earlier in the planning stage. Can I ask you too write a helper method, maybe called `validateRestoreOptions` that we call even before we call `doRestorePlan`. This method can check both `into_db` and `new_db_name` and fail the restore much earlier.

i've added this check to the plan hook function, though i didn't make it its own helper function, in order to follow the style of other checks on the `restoreStmt.Options` features in the planHook (e.g. `Options.EncryptionPassphrase`). Further, we currently have no checks on `Options.IntoDB` that can be done  in the planHook (i.e. before generating the descriptor arrays, sqlDescs and restoreDBs)
nice test cleanup. Some formatting still looks off so I think the linter will shout at you.

In the test below let's also create a table in the db, and insert a few rows. Post restore lets `SELECT count(*)` on the table and verify that we see the same number of rows.

Some more tests I think we should add, probably as subtests (see t.Run() method in other tests):

- Option being incorrectly used in full cluster restore, table restore, multiple target DB restore.
